Interface Subscriber<T>

Type Parameters:
T - the type of values delivered to this subscriber
All Known Implementing Classes:
ConfiguredSubscriber
Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface Subscriber<T>
Callback-style observer for values delivered by a substrate primitive subscription. Implement onNext(Object) to handle each delivered value; the remaining methods fire on terminal or exceptional events and default to no-ops.

Because Subscriber is a FunctionalInterface, a plain lambda targeting onNext is sufficient for the simplest use case: 

Subscriber<String> sub = value -> System.out.println("Got: " + value);

For richer lifecycle handling, use the SubscriberConfig customizer pattern via a primitive's subscribe method: 

atom.subscribe(snapshot, cfg -> cfg
    .onNext(snap -> process(snap))
    .onExpired(() -> reconnect())
    .onError(err -> log.error("boom", err)));

When each method fires

  • onNext(Object) — each time a new value is available
  • onCompleted() — the primitive completed naturally (journal drained, mailbox delivered)
  • onExpired() — the primitive's TTL elapsed without renewal
  • onDeleted() — the primitive was explicitly deleted
  • onCancelled() — the local subscription was torn down (user cancel() or shutdown coordinator); the underlying primitive is unaffected
  • onError(Throwable) — an unexpected exception occurred in the feeder
